For an anchored positive convex representation using only J, the combined deepest mark remains deepest. Any closed base halfspace containing its base contains an input base and hence has weight at least the minimum of finitely many input depths strictly above Q. The resulting base lies in J. For an A-only representation the frozen heredity lemma excludes a target in J, giving A closure.

An integer midpoint of same-parity A sites lies in A by completeness. The accepted atomic compression therefore gives exact weighted Q caps, distinct exclusive-witness parities, and strict exclusion of the other retained caps at each witness. Its depth measure is computed over all original positive weighted sites.

Every retained Q cap excludes each J site by the strict base gap. If a witness and a J site had the same parity, their midpoint would belong to I by lattice completeness and lie strictly outside all retained caps, because the witness is at equality or below while the J site is strictly below every threshold. The A cover forces that midpoint into J, contradicting the frozen heredity property with the witness as a positive atomic input.

The cap union bound gives V_A≤mQ and the strict quota applies to the nonempty proper closed minor J when A and J coexist. Subtracting yields the strict exterior-mass bound. If I=P, Q/M<1/k(P) makes the right side positive when m≥1 by m+k(J)≤k(P). If J is empty, the atomic cover gives M≤mQ<M. Taking m=0 for empty A is consistent.
